prompt: Gorrask: Legend on this rock says a stone-crab grew so vast and so old that it no longer fits inside any canyon it did not carve itself. Whatever the truth of that, a gorrask this big has never needed to hurry: it moves once, settles for a season, and the pool truce holds around it exactly as it holds around everything smaller. Its shell is old enough that whole weep-mat colonies have taken root along the seams. It is NOT an Earth animal: shell shows deep seams between its plates, with weep-mat colonies rooted and growing along those seams; the carapace looks like weathered stone, not glossy crab chitin; the shell is so worn and old that it reads as an ancient rock formation, not a living crab's smooth shell; colossal, landform-scale bulk that dwarfs everything around it, more like a hill or canyon boulder than an animal; sits low and fully settled in place, like a fixed part of the terrain, not raised up on its legs. The body rests close to the ground with compressed walking-leg joints and a broad, settled silhouette while retaining its enormous stone shell and pincers. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.

Ssurr: A hound-sized reptile with one enormous half-circle crest-fan folded flat or blazing open — closed it is a blade, open it is a wheel. Its breeding displays happen at the pools, harmless and spectacular; the fan doubles as its dew-comb on the weeping faces, so courtship and drinking are the same gesture. The tamable charmer of the biome. It is NOT an Earth animal: a single enormous half-circle crest-fan as the dominant structure, not a neck collar or ruff around the throat; when open the fan reads as a wheel: a rigid half-circle disc with radiating spokes, far larger than the head; when folded the fan lies flat into one straight blade-like edge along the body; the fan's rim or spokes carry fine comb-like tines (its dew-comb), so the fan has a toothed edge, not a smooth membrane; hound-sized and hound-proportioned reptile body, not a small slender lizard. Give the animal one anatomically consistent crest-fan whose attachment, plane and projected width rotate with the body across all facings. Carry the same turquoise dorsal coloration and cream underside consistently around the head, back, haunches and tail in every facing. Show a single enormous half-circle crest attached along a consistent body axis, with its attachment visibly distinct from a throat ruff. Equip the fan rim or spokes with a clearly visible row of closely spaced fine comb-like tines. Give the south face natural reptilian eye proportions, restrained brow shapes and a neutral anatomical mouth within the existing painterly treatment. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.

prompt: Shadefern: A deep-green fern growing only on the shaded face of standing stone, every frond swept to the cold side as if combed, its pale rachis catching what light bounces in. Marks which side of a rock is the cold side at a glance -- the stone-shade fern niche, now donor-free under its own name. It is NOT an Earth animal: grows from a vertical face of standing stone, not from soil or ground; every frond swept to one side in parallel, as if combed, not a radiating rosette; pale, light-catching rachis (frond midribs) standing out against the deep-green leaflets; deep-green fronds lying on the shaded side of the rock. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.

Rockfinger: A gnarled, wind-stripped hardwood rooted in the rim cracks of the tall stone, branches clawing out over the drop, bark pale as the stone it grips. At this biome's low sun its shadow runs down the rock face and across the ground for many times its height -- you meet the shadow before the tree. Scarce, and hardy the way it has to be. Slow, scattered, precious timber in high stone country; a felled rockfinger is a caravan event. It is NOT an Earth animal: rooted directly in a crack in a vertical stone cliff rim, not standing in soil on flat ground; branches reaching out sideways over the drop like grasping, claw-like fingers instead of a rounded or conical crown; bark as pale as the surrounding stone, nearly the same colour as the rock it grips; a very long shadow cast down the rock face and across the ground, many times the tree's own height. The tree retains its pale wind-stripped trunk and clawing branches while showing a distinctive invented leaf shape and growth arrangement that remains visible at normal play size. The tree retains its pale, wind-stripped hardwood trunk while showing a distinctive alien branch structure and foliage silhouette recognizable at normal play scale. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.

Jungle Rancor: Jungle rancors were a colossal subspecies of the more common rancor that had evolved on the planet Felucia, but existed on other worlds through suspected "exotic egg sales" and poaching. This subspecies had extreme sexual dimorphism, with the males (referred to as "rancor bulls") being pale whitish grey, having 4 short facial-tusks used for display and an elongated tail for balance. The females were a regal shade of navy blue with webbed hands and had additional layers of thick almost testudine-like growths on their backs (presumably to help avoid predation as juveniles). It's believed this subspecies of rancor was able to grow too such colossal sizes due to it's consumption of the local "fungal trees" on their native Felucia, supplementing it's otherwise carnivorous diet in times of prey sparsity. All facings have charcoal-to-dark-brown armor and arms, a pale tan or ochre underside, and rust-red spike tips. The creature's entire palette uses charcoal, brown, tan, ochre, ivory and rust tones. The hands have clearly visible skin membranes connecting the bases and lower lengths of the clawed fingers.
